# symcompR: Symbolic Computation in R

***symcompR*** is a computer algebra system written in R. It is a native
port of the Python library [SymPy](https://www.sympy.org): expressions
are R objects, exact integers and rationals come from
[gmp](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=gmp), and every algorithm runs
in R. There is no Python, no `reticulate`, and no compiled code.

Results follow SymPy closely, down to the order in which terms print, so
code and answers move between the two systems with little translation.
Outputs are checked against SymPy itself (see
[Validation](#validation)).

symcompR covers exact arithmetic and automatic simplification,
assumptions, differentiation, series and limits, integration and
integral transforms, polynomial algebra and factorization, algebraic
number theory, equation, inequality, ODE, PDE, recurrence and
Diophantine solvers, matrices and matrix expressions, number theory,
combinatorics and group theory, logic, sets, geometry, vectors, tensors,
physical units, parsers for SymPy, LaTeX and Mathematica input, and
printers for LaTeX, MathML, two dimensional text, and code in thirteen
languages.

## Installation

``` r

# Development version
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("adamrsophie/symcompR")
```

symcompR needs R 4.3.0 or later and the `gmp` package. It contains no
compiled code, so no C or C++ toolchain is required.

## Quick start

``` r

library(symcompR)
x <- Symbol("x"); y <- Symbol("y")
n <- Symbol("n", integer = TRUE)
f <- Function("f")

expand((x + y)^3)
#> x^3 + 3*x^2*y + 3*x*y^2 + y^3

sym_factor(x^4 - 1)
#> (x - 1)*(x + 1)*(x^2 + 1)

diff(sin(x) * exp(x), x)
#> exp(x)*sin(x) + exp(x)*cos(x)

sym_integrate(exp(-x^2), list(x, -Inf, Inf))
#> sqrt(pi)

limit(sin(x) / x, x, 0)
#> 1

series(tan(x), x, 0, 8)
#> x + x^3/3 + 2*x^5/15 + 17*x^7/315 + O(x^8)

solveset(sin(x) - Rational(1, 2), x, Reals)
#> Union(ImageSet(Lambda(_n, 2*_n*pi + pi/6), Integers), ImageSet(Lambda(_n, 2*_n*pi + 5*pi/6), Integers))

dsolve(Eq(diff(f(x), x, 2) + f(x), 0), f(x))
#> Eq(f(x), C1*sin(x) + C2*cos(x))

summation(1/n^2, list(n, 1, Inf))
#> pi^2/6

M <- Matrix(list(list(1, 2), list(3, 4)))
inverse(M)
#> Matrix(2, 2)
#> [-2 , 1   ]
#> [3/2, -1/2]

latex(Integral(exp(-x^2), list(x, -Inf, Inf)))
#> \int\limits_{- \infty}^{\infty} e^{- x^{2}}\, dx

ccode(sqrt(x) + Rational(1, 3))
#> sqrt(x) + 1.0/3.0

pprint((x + 1)/(y - 2) + sqrt(x^2 + 1), use_unicode = FALSE)
#>            ________
#> x + 1     /  2
#> ----- + \/  x  + 1
#> y - 2
```

## What is covered

| Area | Highlights |
|----|----|
| Core | Exact `Integer` and `Rational` arithmetic, canonical `Add`/`Mul`/`Pow`, assumptions, `subs`, `xreplace`, `expand` and its hints, `factor_terms`, arbitrary precision evaluation with [`N()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/symcompR/reference/N.md) |
| Functions | Elementary, gamma family, error and exponential integrals, zeta, Bessel, Airy, elliptic, orthogonal polynomials, `Piecewise`, B-splines |
| Calculus | `diff`, `limit`, `series`, `summation`, `product`, finite differences, singularities, extrema, monotonicity, periodicity, `AccumBounds` interval arithmetic, `not_empty_in` |
| Integration | Heuristic and rational function integration, definite integrals, Laplace, Fourier, Mellin, sine, cosine and Hankel transforms |
| Polynomials | Sparse polynomials over QQ and GF(p), factorization (Zassenhaus, Hensel, Wang’s multivariate EEZ, algebraic and Gaussian domains), GCDs, Groebner bases, resultants, roots to degree four, `CRootOf`, `galois_group` to degree six |
| Algebraic number theory | Number fields, `round_two` integral bases, `prime_decomp`, `prime_valuation`, `PrimeIdeal` |
| Solvers | `solve`, `solveset` with periodic families, linear and polynomial systems, inequalities, `dsolve`, `pdsolve`, `rsolve`, `diophantine`, `nsolve` |
| Simplification | `simplify`, `trigsimp`, the Fu et al. trigonometric rules (`fu`, `TR0` to `TR22`), `powsimp`, `radsimp`, `signsimp`, `collect`, `nsimplify`, `gammasimp`, `hypersimp` |
| Matrices | Dense symbolic matrices, determinants, inverses, eigenvalues, Jordan form, LU, QR, Cholesky, Hermite and Smith normal forms; matrix expressions (`MatrixSymbol`, `BlockMatrix`, `MatrixSlice`, `blockcut`, `block_collapse`) |
| Number theory | Primality, `factorint` (Pollard rho and p - 1, ECM, quadratic sieve), residues, discrete logarithms, CRT, continued fractions |
| Sets and logic | Intervals, finite sets, `ImageSet`, `ConditionSet`, `Range`, ordinals; normal forms, Quine-McCluskey, DPLL satisfiability; assumptions with `ask`, `refine`, and `assuming` |
| Series objects | Sequences, linear recurrences, Pade approximants, Fourier series |
| Combinatorics and groups | Permutations, permutation groups (Schreier-Sims, Sylow subgroups, cosets), free and finitely presented groups (Todd-Coxeter, Reidemeister-Schreier, rewriting systems, homomorphisms), polycyclic groups, polyhedra |
| Vectors and tensors | `sympy.vector` (`CoordSys3D`, del operators, dyadics, parametric regions and integrals), tensor canonicalization (`canon_bp`), `TensorHead` algebra, `PartialDerivative`, arrays |
| Physics | `sympy.physics.units`: unit systems (SI, MKS, MKSA, natural, CGS Gauss), `convert_to`, dimensional analysis, physical constants |
| Parsing | `parse_expr` with SymPy’s transformations, `parse_latex`, `parse_mathematica` |
| Other modules | Geometry in 2D and 3D, statistics, discrete transforms, quaternions, plotting |
| Printing | `str`, `srepr`, LaTeX, MathML, 2D pretty printing, `TableForm`, and code for C, C++, Fortran, JavaScript, Julia, Mathematica, Maple, Octave, R, Python, Rust, GLSL, and SMT-LIB |

Coverage is a work in progress: 867 of the 901 names in SymPy’s top
level API (96 percent) are available, counted by name. A ported function
can still handle fewer input classes than its SymPy counterpart. Python
classes and exceptions with no R meaning (`Basic`, `Expr`,
`PolynomialError`, domain objects such as `ZZ`) are not planned.

## Differences from SymPy

- Powers print and parse as `^`, not `**`.
- `==` is structural equality, as in SymPy; build equations with
  [`Eq()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/symcompR/reference/Eq.md).
- Write `Rational(1, 3)`, not `1/3`: R evaluates `1/3` to a double
  first.
- Floats have arbitrary precision, as in SymPy: `N(sym_pi, 50)` gives 50
  significant digits, and the default is 15.
- Constants whose names clash with R are `sym_pi`, `sym_E`, and `sym_I`.
- Attaching symcompR masks no base R function, and a test enforces this.
  SymPy names that clash with base R carry a `sym_` prefix:
  [`sym_factor()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/symcompR/reference/sym_factor.md),
  [`sym_integrate()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/symcompR/reference/sym_integrate.md),
  [`sym_symbols()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/symcompR/reference/Symbol.md),
  [`sym_var()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/symcompR/reference/Symbol.md),
  [`sym_det()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/symcompR/reference/sym_det.md),
  [`sym_factorial()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/symcompR/reference/special-functions.md),
  [`sym_beta()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/symcompR/reference/special-functions.md),
  [`sym_binomial()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/symcompR/reference/special-functions.md),
  [`sym_atan2()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/symcompR/reference/elementary-functions.md),
  [`sym_Mod()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/symcompR/reference/elementary-functions.md)
  (or `x %% y`),
  [`sym_ordered()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/symcompR/reference/core-helpers.md),
  [`sym_poly()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/symcompR/reference/poly-aliases.md),
  [`sym_rf()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/symcompR/reference/function-aliases.md),
  [`sym_lcm()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/symcompR/reference/gcd.md),
  [`sym_fft()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/symcompR/reference/convolution.md),
  [`sym_decompose()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/symcompR/reference/polys-extra.md),
  [`sym_trunc()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/symcompR/reference/polys-extra.md),
  [`sym_prod()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/symcompR/reference/misc-helpers.md),
  [`sym_reshape()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/symcompR/reference/misc-helpers.md),
  [`sym_diag()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/symcompR/reference/matrix-builders.md),
  and
  [`sym_trace()`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/symcompR/reference/matrix-builders.md).
  Where base R has a generic (`diff`, `sin`, `exp`, `pretty`, `scale`,
  `t`, …), symcompR adds an S3 method instead.

## Validation

- Expected values in the test suite come from SymPy, pinned to commit
  `86150a81`, run as an oracle on the same inputs.
- Larger modules have dedicated differential test harnesses against
  SymPy: the Diophantine solver matches SymPy on 52 of 53 equations (the
  last differs only in its error message), and the number theory module
  is compared function by function.
- `R CMD check --as-cran` passes with no errors, warnings, or notes.

## Citing symcompR

``` r

citation("symcompR")
```

The repository ships machine readable citation and software metadata for
FAIR harvesters:

- [`CITATION.cff`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/symcompR/CITATION.cff):
  Citation File Format (GitHub “Cite this repository”, Zenodo).
- [`codemeta.json`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/symcompR/codemeta.json):
  CodeMeta 2.0 software metadata crosswalk.
- [`.zenodo.json`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/symcompR/.zenodo.json):
  Zenodo deposit metadata (author, license, related identifiers).
- [`ro-crate-metadata.json`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/symcompR/ro-crate-metadata.json):
  RO-Crate 1.1 packaging and provenance.
- `inst/CITATION`: the R level citation (`citation("symcompR")`).
- `inst/COPYRIGHTS` and `inst/SYMPY-LICENSE`: provenance and the license
  of the ported SymPy code.

All carry the GPL-3.0 SPDX identifier, the author, and the SymPy
provenance. Once the first GitHub release is archived on Zenodo, its
concept DOI will resolve to the latest release.

## Contributing

Bug reports, feature requests, and pull requests are welcome; see
[`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/symcompR/CONTRIBUTING.md).
A wrong answer is the most useful bug report: include the input and, if
you can, what SymPy returns for it. Please follow the [Code of
Conduct](https://adamrsophie.github.io/symcompR/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md), and
report security issues privately as described in
[`SECURITY.md`](https://adamrsophie.github.io/symcompR/SECURITY.md).
